core_obligations: Simplicity (proof lines 582-584): the tensor product of the algebra with its opposite is simple by the cited lemma.
Injectivity (proof lines 584-588): the natural map sending a tensor to the endomorphism multiplying on the left and on the right is a nonzero algebra map out of a simple algebra, hence injective.

Dimension count (proof lines 589-590): both source and target have the same dimension over the ground field, so the injective map is an isomorphism, and the target is a matrix algebra of the size displayed.
proof_roadmap: Use simplicity of the tensor product with the opposite algebra.
Show the natural map into the endomorphism algebra is injective.
Compare dimensions to conclude that it is an isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a finite central simple algebra tensored with its opposite algebra is a matrix algebra of size the degree of the algebra (statement lines 575-580). The proof is a complete argument: the tensor product with the opposite is simple by a named lemma (proof lines 582-584), the natural map into the endomorphism algebra of the algebra as a vector space is injective because its source is simple (proof lines 584-588), and a dimension count makes it an isomorphism, the target being a matrix algebra (proof lines 589-590). The non-formal content is the injectivity from simplicity and the dimension count. The claim is H2.
